constraints: The signature must remain bound to the exact revision.

feedback.reason: The signer must reach revision text before signing and invoke a keyboard- or switch-operable action that reports its result.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A focus order that follows the document lets the signer inspect its revision before reaching Sign. The signature action must identify the same revision currently under review.
details.scenarioApplication: A signer opens and signs the current document revision. Which navigation and signing controls let keyboard or switch users review the same revision and complete its signature? The signature must remain bound to the exact revision. Review and signing actions must both be available without pointer-only controls.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Keyboard access does not authorize signing; preserve explicit user activation and server-side revision binding.
details.errorCorrection: A pointer-only page reveal blocks keyboard and switch review; a sign control without a readable result also leaves rejection unclear. Keep review and activation available as separate steps.
details.transfer: If a newer revision arrives while the signer is reviewing, move the review context to that version only after the signer chooses it; do not sign an unseen revision.

messages.text: Requiring pointer selection to reveal each page body prevents keyboard and switch users from reviewing the revision.
Moving focus to Sign before review skips the revision details the signer must inspect.
Choose how keyboard or switch users reach and read the revision before activation.
A keyboard shortcut does not help a switch user, and a pointer-only commit prevents the same action from being completed without a pointer.
A signed icon without an announced completed or rejected result leaves a screen-reader user unable to confirm the outcome.
Choose a named operable signing control and a perceivable result for both acceptance and rejection.

values.text: Keep revision text in order, but require pointer selection to expose a page body.
Keep revision text in reading order and let keyboard or switch users review before signing.
Keep revision details keyboard-readable, but focus Sign before the signer reviews them.
Offer a named shortcut for signing, but require a pointer to commit the signature.
Allow keyboard activation and show a signed icon, but expose rejection only by its color state.
Provide a named sign action and announce the completed or rejected signature result.

prompt: A signer opens and signs the current document revision. Which controls let a keyboard or switch user review the revision and complete the same signing action?

constraints: Camera access and network delivery can fail independently.
Keyboard and switch users must be able to select a file and retry without losing acknowledged transfer state.

feedback.reason: Use a labeled file input, retain the selected file and upload session for retry, and report pending, failed, or confirmed completion.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A native file input exposes selection to keyboard and switch activation. The upload session owns acknowledged bytes, so a retry resumes that transfer rather than creating a second draft.
details.scenarioApplication: Camera permission is denied and the connection drops once during transfer. Which input path lets the technician choose a file without the camera and recover the same upload? Camera access and network delivery can fail independently. Keyboard and switch users must be able to select a file and retry without losing acknowledged transfer state.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Choosing a file is not delivery: keep the transfer pending or failed until the server confirms completion, and do not discard the selected file when connectivity drops.
details.errorCorrection: A reachable camera button still cannot provide a file when permission is denied.
details.transfer: If the camera later becomes available but the network is still down, preserve the pending file and session; changing input source must not claim the upload completed.

messages.text: A reachable camera button still cannot provide a file when permission is denied.
A parallel draft can diverge from the interrupted upload; both sources should enter the same recoverable task state.
Focus alone does not activate file selection; expose a real keyboard-operable chooser and retry path.

options.text: Use a labeled file chooser accessible by keyboard or switch; retain its upload session on retry and report each transfer state.
Keep capture as the only source but expose its button to keyboard and switch; allow file selection later by pointer.
Offer a keyboard-accessible chooser, but start a new upload session on retry and leave prior progress unresolved.
Keep a labeled drop zone and keyboard activation, but restart from byte zero after every reconnect.

prompt: Camera permission is denied and the connection drops once during transfer. Which input path lets the technician choose a file without the camera and recover the same upload?

constraints: Names and translated labels can expand beyond English widths.
Errors must identify fields and remain actionable; confirmation must reflect the server result.

feedback.reason: Associate each error with its field; after submit, keep focus or move it to a linked summary, then announce the confirmed result.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Programmatic field-error association links each message to the input; a focused summary can provide direct links when several fields fail. Focus should move once in response to submit, not on every render.
details.scenarioApplication: An attendee submits a registration with a long localized name and receives field errors. Which recovery keeps every invalid field reachable by keyboard or switch and confirms the final result? Names and translated labels can expand beyond English widths. Errors must identify fields and remain actionable; confirmation must reflect the server result.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Allow the form to grow for translated names. Keep invalid state until corrected, and report registration success only after the server accepts it.
details.errorCorrection: A summary without field links announces the problem but adds a second search task, especially in a long form.
details.transfer: If a server-side validation error arrives after the attendee has moved to another field, announce the update without repeatedly stealing focus and provide a direct route back to the rejected value.

messages.text: A summary without field links announces the problem but adds a second search task, especially in a long form.
Repeated focus changes interrupt correction and can make a switch user lose their current position.
Color does not name the error, and leaving focus at Submit supplies no route to the affected field.

options.text: Focus a concise summary, but make its entries plain text so users must search the form for each invalid field.
Link each field error, then move focus through every invalid field again whenever validation rerenders.
Keep focus on Submit and mark errors with color, relying on the attendee to locate the invalid value.
Link each error to its field; focus or link a concise summary, then announce the confirmed result.

prompt: An attendee submits a registration with a long localized name and receives field errors. Which recovery keeps every invalid field reachable by keyboard or switch and confirms the final result?

constraints: Assignment, exposure, rollback, and telemetry have distinct meanings.
The server authorizes changes and confirms whether rollback succeeded.

feedback.reason: Use named assignment and rollback controls, expose cohort and exposure state, and show the server-confirmed outcome.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Named controls expose each operation to sequential input; the visible cohort and exposure identify the target, while the response determines the authoritative rollback state.
details.scenarioApplication: A product engineer changes a cohort assignment, inspects exposure, and may roll back an experiment. Which console interaction supports keyboard and switch operation while preserving the server’s rollout decision? Assignment, exposure, rollback, and telemetry have distinct meanings. The server authorizes changes and confirms whether rollback succeeded.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Input accessibility does not grant rollout permission. Keep pending, rejected, and confirmed states distinct and correlate them to the same cohort and experiment IDs.
details.errorCorrection: Focus does not provide the move operation; assignment needs an equivalent non-drag action.
details.transfer: If rollback is rejected while the engineer switches input modes, keep the cohort selected, preserve the assignment, and expose the rejection with an actionable retry or explanation.

messages.text: Focus does not provide the move operation; assignment needs an equivalent non-drag action.
A local optimistic label can imply the rollout changed when the server may reject the request.
Separate state can disagree with the live cohort and telemetry shown to pointer users.

options.text: Keep the cohort row focusable and show its exposure, but require a drag to change assignment.
Provide named keyboard actions and visible cohort state, but label rollback complete before server confirmation.
Expose named assignment and rollback actions; show cohort, exposure, and the confirmed server outcome.
Provide the same named actions in a keyboard console, but keep its cohort state separate from the live console.

prompt: A product engineer changes a cohort assignment, inspects exposure, and may roll back an experiment. Which console interaction supports keyboard and switch operation while preserving the server’s rollout decision?

constraints: A selectable destination must be available without dragging or map panning.
The selected stop shown in the list and map must identify the same destination.

feedback.reason: A named destination list provides selection without panning, and its selected stop can stay synchronized with the map.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A named destination list provides a focusable selection action; synchronizing the chosen stop label with the map marker makes the selected place verifiable without panning.
details.scenarioApplication: A dispatcher adjusts a route while live vehicle positions update. Which map controls allow keyboard or switch users to select a destination and verify the chosen stop? A selectable destination must be available without dragging or map panning. The selected stop shown in the list and map must identify the same destination.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The map remains a useful overview, but destination selection cannot depend on pointer movement across the canvas.
details.errorCorrection: Panning or dragging may move the map but does not select a destination through sequential keyboard or switch input.
details.transfer: If live positions update after a stop is selected, keep the destination selection stable and update vehicle markers independently.

messages.text: Single-pointer selection is an alternative input, but does not satisfy keyboard or switch selection.
Panning changes the map viewport; it does not select a named destination through sequential input.
This decision is required because A selectable destination must be available without dragging or map panning.
A color-only marker does not identify the chosen stop to all users.
A stale marker breaks the required relationship between the selected result and the map.
This decision is required because The selected stop shown in the list and map must identify the same destination.

values.text: Show named stops and support switch scanning, but require a pointer to commit selection.
Offer focusable destinations that keyboard or switch users can select by name.
Let keyboard users traverse map controls, then pan the viewport to reach a stop before selection.
Show the selected stop in map and list, but indicate the map selection by color alone.
Name the selected result in the list, but keep the former stop emphasized as the map recenters.
Show the selected stop by name and synchronize that selection with its map marker.

prompt: A dispatcher adjusts a route while live vehicle positions update. Which map controls allow keyboard or switch users to select a destination and verify the chosen stop?

constraints: Filters belong to the current view and must be shareable without becoming global application state.
Reorder submission and its result are separate from filter selection.

feedback.reason: Use labeled filters mirrored in the URL, show the active-filter summary, and keep reorder as a separate confirmed action.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A labeled control updates view state; serializing shareable criteria in the URL lets another session reconstruct that view. A distinct submit action commits the reorder and reports its own result.
details.scenarioApplication: A store manager filters inventory, shares the view, and submits a reorder. Which keyboard and switch path preserves reviewable filters and restores the same criteria from a shared link? Filters belong to the current view and must be shareable without becoming global application state. Reorder submission and its result are separate from filter selection.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Browser history and links represent filter intent, not a successful reorder. Preserve the visible active-filter summary even when the URL restores the criteria.
details.errorCorrection: Copying only the path loses the selected criteria when another user opens the link.
details.transfer: If a shared URL is opened with one unavailable filter value, retain the supported criteria, explain the unavailable value, and leave reorder unsubmitted.

messages.text: Copying only the path loses the selected criteria when another user opens the link.
Focus is for navigation, not an implicit state-changing submit; the manager cannot review that operation safely.
A second panel state can disagree with the view and cannot reproduce the filter set from its link.

options.text: Expose labeled filters in the URL and a visible summary; submit reorder separately and report its result.
Show labeled filters and a summary, but keep selections local so a copied link opens the unfiltered view.
Mirror filters in the URL and show a summary, but apply changes when controls receive focus.
Provide a keyboard filter panel and URL state, but keep panel selections separate from the visible inventory.

prompt: A store manager filters inventory, shares the view, and submits a reorder. Which keyboard and switch path preserves reviewable filters and restores the same criteria from a shared link?

constraints: Keyboard, switch, and single-pointer users need an equivalent card-move operation.
Reconnect may reveal a newer remote version that conflicts with the facilitator’s pending move.

feedback.reason: Select the card, choose a destination with labeled controls, and show a conflict instead of silently replacing either version.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A destination control performs the same move without dragging. Reconnect compares versions; when both sides changed, retain the local draft and latest remote state as a conflict for explicit resolution.
details.scenarioApplication: A facilitator moves a card on a collaborative board while remote updates may arrive after reconnect. Which non-drag input path preserves local intent and makes a conflict visible? Keyboard, switch, and single-pointer users need an equivalent card-move operation. Reconnect may reveal a newer remote version that conflicts with the facilitator’s pending move.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The control supplies input equivalence but does not determine merge policy. Do not claim the card moved until the chosen resolution is accepted and the resulting column is known.
details.errorCorrection: A focusable card still has no non-drag operation for choosing its destination.
details.transfer: If reconnect reports no competing change, commit the staged destination normally; if the version differs, keep the facilitator’s selection visible while asking them to resolve it.

messages.text: A focusable card still has no non-drag operation for choosing its destination.
Silently preferring remote state discards a deliberate local action and gives no chance to resolve it.
Unconditionally preferring local state can overwrite a collaborator’s newer move; expose the conflict and preserve both intents.

options.text: Make each card focusable and show its column, but keep dragging as the only move operation.
Offer a keyboard destination menu, but silently replace the local move with a newer remote version.
Keep the local move after reconnect, but overwrite the remote version without showing the conflict.
Choose a card destination through labeled controls; retain local intent and show a version conflict for resolution.

prompt: A facilitator moves a card on a collaborative board while remote updates may arrive after reconnect. Which non-drag input path preserves local intent and makes a conflict visible?

constraints: The file must be selectable without pointer input.
Sensitive document fields stay outside third-party access and need not be echoed in progress messages.

feedback.reason: Use a labeled native file chooser and local status that names only necessary metadata; keep document fields away from third-party scripts.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The native chooser supplies keyboard selection; a local upload state can report progress without exposing document fields to analytics. Minimize the visible metadata to what the case worker needs.
details.scenarioApplication: A case worker uploads a confidential document. Keyboard selection is required, while third-party scripts must never receive its fields. Which flow provides useful progress without crossing that data boundary? The file must be selectable without pointer input. Sensitive document fields stay outside third-party access and need not be echoed in progress messages.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Accessibility does not require copying sensitive values into announcements. Keep the file payload and fields within the authorized upload path; completion still depends on server confirmation.
details.errorCorrection: A focusable drop zone still lacks keyboard activation for selecting a file.
details.transfer: If the worker selects a second file after the first fails, retain distinct local identities and statuses without sending either document’s fields to a third-party script.

messages.text: A focusable drop zone still lacks keyboard activation for selecting a file.
Removing data later does not undo the disclosure to third-party code during preview.
Suppressing every status protects content but leaves the worker unable to identify a file or recover from failure.

options.text: Make the drop zone keyboard-focusable, but leave file selection available only by pointer.
Use keyboard file selection and local progress, but send document fields to analytics before deleting them.
Use a labeled native chooser and local progress status; keep document fields out of third-party scripts.
Keep fields private and offer keyboard file selection, but hide filename, progress, and recovery status.

prompt: A case worker uploads a confidential document. Keyboard selection is required, while third-party scripts must never receive its fields. Which flow provides useful progress without crossing that data boundary?

constraints: RTL direction and plural categories depend on the content locale.
Translated text can expand; focus and actions must remain available without clipping.

feedback.reason: The editor must preserve RTL navigation, locale plural grammar, expansion, and its keyboard action path together.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Direction controls text flow and caret behavior; locale message rules select plural forms, while flexible sizing lets the resulting translation grow without displacing editor actions.
details.scenarioApplication: A translator edits a long message after changing locale. Which editor contract preserves RTL navigation, locale-aware plural wording, and expanded text while supporting keyboard and switch input? RTL direction and plural categories depend on the content locale. Translated text can expand; focus and actions must remain available without clipping.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Text direction, grammatical formatting, and focus order are separate concerns: changing one must not corrupt the message or remove controls.
details.errorCorrection: Stable focus alone does not ensure correct RTL caret behavior, plural grammar, or room for the expanded translation.
details.transfer: If the same editor switches to a locale with longer plural forms, preserve the message arguments and focus target while recalculating the text and allowing it to wrap.

messages.text: Alignment does not change caret direction; the RTL editor needs logical text navigation.
Reversing characters mutates the stored message and is not a bidi rendering strategy.
This decision is required because RTL direction and plural categories depend on the content locale.
Localized digits do not change English-only plural grammar.
One fixed noun form can be grammatically wrong for the locale’s plural categories.
This decision is required because RTL direction and plural categories depend on the content locale.
Keeping focus order does not recover translation text clipped to English dimensions.
A content-length change should not move focus away from the active editing task.
This decision is required because RTL direction and plural categories depend on the content locale.

values.text: Align RTL copy right, but preserve left-to-right caret movement in the editor.
Set direction from the content locale and preserve logical caret movement for the editor.
Keep source text intact and set RTL direction, but leave arrow-key caret movement unchanged.
Format counts locally, but keep English singular/plural message branches.
Use locale plural categories, but keep one noun form and append the numeral.
Select message form from locale plural rules and pass the count as a message argument.
Let translated text wrap while editor actions remain in their logical focus order.
Keep editor actions in logical focus order, but clamp translated copy to English height.
Let the message wrap and expand, but move focus to actions when the editor height changes.

prompt: A translator edits a long message after changing locale. Which editor contract preserves RTL navigation, locale-aware plural wording, and expanded text while supporting keyboard and switch input?

constraints: The applicant must know whether the primary submission succeeded.
A rejected request stays recoverable and must not look like a completed application.

feedback.reason: Keep the missing-document field reachable, link its error to the field, and show the rejected server result with a correction path.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Field association tells the user what failed; a direct keyboard route lets them correct it. The submitted/failed state comes from the server response, not from leaving the form.
details.scenarioApplication: A permitting coordinator requests a missing document, then the server rejects the submission. Which keyboard behavior identifies the error and supports correction without presenting the application as complete? The applicant must know whether the primary submission succeeded. A rejected request stays recoverable and must not look like a completed application.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A rejection is not a successful application and should not erase the entered values. Keep unrelated fields intact while the missing document is supplied.
details.errorCorrection: A banner without field association can announce rejection but cannot guide correction; repeated focus moves also interrupt the task.
details.transfer: If the server rejects a different field after resubmission, identify that field and update the failure message without clearing the corrected document.

messages.text: A banner without field association can announce rejection but cannot guide correction; repeated focus moves also interrupt the task.
The server has rejected the request, so closing and announcing completion reports a false result.
A rejection requires a repair path; disabling all controls prevents the coordinator from supplying the missing document.

options.text: Link rejection to the missing-document field and keep that field reachable with a correction action.
Show the server rejection in a banner and focus it, but leave the field unmarked and repeat focus on rerender.
Keep a keyboard path to the field, but close the form and announce completion after any response.
Identify the missing field and server rejection, but disable the form instead of allowing correction.

prompt: A permitting coordinator requests a missing document, then the server rejects the submission. Which keyboard behavior identifies the error and supports correction without presenting the application as complete?

constraints: Playback capability can be unavailable in the current browser state.
The player must not displace metadata that identifies the shared lesson.

feedback.reason: Keep lesson metadata before named playback controls; expose start, pause, resume, and unavailable state through keyboard operation.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Sequential focus lets the learner read the shared lesson identity before choosing a playback action. Distinct controls expose state transitions; unavailable means no playback began.
details.scenarioApplication: A learner opens a lesson from a shared link. Playback depends on browser availability, and the lesson title must remain available in the first view. The player must not displace metadata that identifies the shared lesson.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not replace metadata with player focus or claim playback started until the browser reports that it is active.
details.errorCorrection: Autoplay can begin before the learner reviews context, and moving focus hides the first-view metadata path.

messages.text: Autoplay can begin before the learner reviews context, and moving focus hides the first-view metadata path.
A timeline can seek but does not necessarily provide distinct, named start/pause actions or an unavailable state.
Hover does not work for keyboard or switch input, and the title should remain reachable.

options.text: Keep named controls available, but autoplay and move focus to the player before the title is reviewed.
Keep title and focus order, but use the timeline as the only way to start, pause, or resume.
Keep playback state labeled, but reveal the controls only on pointer hover.
Keep the lesson title before named playback controls; expose start, pause, resume, and unavailable states.

prompt: A learner opens a lesson from a shared link. Playback depends on browser availability, and the lesson title must remain available in the first view. Which controls support keyboard or switch start, pause, and resume?

constraints: Preview and checks do not grant publishing authority.

feedback.reason: Keep Preview, checks, and Publish as separate named actions; show check results and the confirmed publish outcome.

Which keyboard behavior preserves a separate authorized Publish action and reports the actual publication result? Preview and checks do not grant publishing authority. The publish operation requires a separate action and server confirmation.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Keyboard activation should match pointer semantics without collapsing preview into publication or bypassing authorization.
details.errorCorrection: Completing a preview is not explicit authorization to publish; Enter should activate only its focused control.

messages.text: Completing a preview is not explicit authorization to publish; Enter should activate only its focused control.
Rendering proves only that preview content loaded, not that the server published it.
A pointer-only check result blocks the required review path and makes Publish less informed.

options.text: Keep Preview and checks named, but let Enter in the preview trigger Publish when content appears complete.
Keep keyboard review of checks, but treat successful preview rendering as reader-visible publication.
Keep Preview, checks, and Publish separate; report publication only after server confirmation.
Keep preview and Publish keyboard-operable, but require a pointer to inspect check results.

constraints: Incoming entries can appear while the current list remains open.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: When the user explicitly opens a new message, focus can move as part of that action; background arrival alone is not an instruction to navigate.
details.errorCorrection: Moving focus to each new entry interrupts reading, while rereading the whole list repeats unchanged content.

messages.text: An announcement may be useful, but forced focus movement interrupts the message currently being read.
Stable focus alone does not provide keyboard or switch navigation to new messages.
This decision is required because Incoming entries can appear while the current list remains open.
Repeating unchanged entries creates redundant speech even if the announcement is concise.
A visible badge without a name or status update is not exposed to a screen reader.
This decision is required because Incoming entries can appear while the current list remains open.

constraints: Recommendations are noncritical to the initial view.

constraints: Keyboard and switch users need a date-edit path without dragging.

constraints: Authorization and audit evidence remain server authoritative.

constraints: Rapid changes must not let an older response overwrite newer intent.

values.text: Expose named query and cancel actions in a visible keyboard order.
Keep query order logical and label Cancel, but remove Cancel from keyboard order while pending.
Name query and cancel actions, but contain focus in results until the request finishes.
Keep results current, but move focus to the first cell after every response.

constraints: Large result sets and map rendering must not block place selection.
Refreshing or windowing results must preserve the active result and its relationship to the map marker.

feedback.reason: The result list should remain usable while map work is pending, and selection needs a stable identity across refresh.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A semantic list exposes each place as a focusable selection. Windowing can bound rendering work, but selection and focus must be keyed to result identity rather than a row’s temporary position.
details.scenarioApplication: A map search returns many places while map rendering competes for device resources. Which result-list design remains keyboard-operable, responsive, and synchronized with the selected marker? Large result sets and map rendering must not block place selection. Refreshing or windowing results must preserve the active result and its relationship to the map marker.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The map is a synchronized visualization, not the only way to reach a result. Keep list selection responsive even when marker rendering is delayed or a large result set is virtualized.
details.errorCorrection: Keeping every row mounted can still block responsiveness; virtualization is safe only when it preserves stable result identity and focus.
details.transfer: If new places arrive before the active result is rendered, retain its identity and restore focus when it returns; do not select a different place at the same row index.

messages.text: A complete DOM list can be accessible, but waiting for every marker couples list responsiveness to map rendering.
A row index can refer to a different place after reordering; preserve the result ID and focused selection.
A responsive canvas still leaves place selection dependent on panning rather than keyboard-operable results.

options.text: Keep every result in the DOM and focusable, but let map rendering delay list updates until all markers finish.
Virtualize result rows for speed, but preserve selection by row index when new results reorder the list.
Keep results as named focusable items independent of map rendering; preserve the active result ID and synchronize its marker.
Keep the map responsive with a canvas layer, but require panning to reach and select each named place.

constraints: The rendered role determines the expected interaction pattern.
Visual token changes must not silently change focus, state, or keyboard behavior.

feedback.reason: Use native behavior when it fits; otherwise implement the role’s full name, state, focus, and keyboard pattern.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A semantic role communicates expected operations and state. Native elements provide much of that contract; custom widgets must implement and test the matching focus and key behavior.
details.scenarioApplication: A shared design-system widget can render as a dialog or combobox while visual tokens evolve. Which contract keeps keyboard behavior and assistive-technology state stable across products? The rendered role determines the expected interaction pattern. Visual token changes must not silently change focus, state, or keyboard behavior.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Choose a role that matches the actual control. Styling may change without changing its role, state transitions, or keyboard pattern.
details.errorCorrection: A role promises behavior; announcing a combobox or dialog without its interaction model misleads assistive technology.
details.transfer: If a visual redesign changes the widget from a dialog to a combobox, revisit the semantic role and interaction pattern together rather than carrying over stale key handling.

messages.text: A role promises behavior; announcing a combobox or dialog without its interaction model misleads assistive technology.
Per-product patterns drift, so users cannot rely on the shared component contract.
A pointer workaround does not satisfy keyboard operation and makes the common component incomplete.

options.text: Keep styling and add the widget role, but leave its keyboard behavior unchanged.
Implement keyboard behavior for each product, but let teams define different focus and key patterns.
Keep shared semantics and state, but remove keyboard operation and document a pointer workaround.
Use native behavior when suitable; otherwise implement the role’s full name, state, focus, and key pattern.

prompt: A shared design-system widget can render as a dialog or combobox while visual tokens evolve. Which contract keeps keyboard behavior and assistive-technology state stable across products?

constraints: Evidence must correlate browser, release, and user impact.
If a filter removes the active row, focus must move predictably and explain the change.

feedback.reason: Use named filters and logical row navigation; preserve the active row when it remains, otherwise move to a nearby valid row with status.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Keep a stable row identity through refresh. If that row disappears under a filter, choose a nearby valid row and announce why focus moved instead of leaving it on a removed element.
details.scenarioApplication: An on-call engineer filters incident evidence by browser and release while reading one impact row. Which keyboard behavior preserves the active row when results refresh? Evidence must correlate browser, release, and user impact. If a filter removes the active row, focus must move predictably and explain the change.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Preserve focus only when the active row still belongs to the result set; retaining a reference to a filtered-out row is not a valid focus target.
details.errorCorrection: Resetting focus discards the engineer’s current context even when that row still exists.
details.transfer: If a later filter removes the current row, move to the next logical result and announce the new context without discarding browser and release criteria.

messages.text: Resetting focus discards the engineer’s current context even when that row still exists.
Color alone supplies neither a named criterion nor a keyboard operation.
Dragging is unnecessary for filtering and does not offer the required keyboard path.

options.text: Keep filters and row names accessible, but move focus to the first result after every refresh.
Keep the table focusable and filters visible, but name filter states only through color.
Use named filters and logical row navigation; retain the active row or move to a valid neighbor with status.
Keep evidence rows keyboard-focusable, but require dragging into browser or release buckets to filter.

prompt: An on-call engineer filters incident evidence by browser and release while reading one impact row. Which keyboard behavior preserves the active row when results refresh?

constraints: A failed confirmation must not look like a completed booking.

feedback.reason: Slot availability guides selection before submit, and a failed confirmation needs a direct recovery path.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Each slot needs an accessible name and availability state before activation. After submit, a server failure must be announced and linked to an action that lets the patient choose again.
details.scenarioApplication: A patient selects a time slot and confirms an appointment. Which keyboard or switch behavior exposes slot availability and makes a failed confirmation recoverable? Unavailable slots must be identifiable before selection. A failed confirmation must not look like a completed booking and must provide a correction path.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Focus may move to a concise error summary after failure, but the summary must identify the failed step and link back to valid controls.
details.errorCorrection: A slot color or generic failed toast does not identify which time is unavailable or how the patient can recover.
details.transfer: If the chosen slot becomes unavailable before the server confirms it, preserve the patient’s context, announce the conflict, and offer current slots.

messages.text: A named slot still needs an availability state that does not rely on color.
A disabled slot without a reason hides why it cannot be selected.
This decision is required because A failed confirmation must not look like a completed booking.
Submission progress is not a recoverable failure result; the patient needs a next action.
Closing the form removes the correction path and implies completion despite the failure.
This decision is required because A failed confirmation must not look like a completed booking.

values.text: Name each slot and expose selection, but distinguish unavailable times only by color.
Disable unavailable slots and retain schedule order, but omit their visible time labels.
Name slots and expose available or unavailable state before keyboard or switch selection.
Keep focus stable and announce submission, but leave focus on a spinner after failure.
Keep focus stable, announce failure, and offer a keyboard-accessible action to choose again.
Preserve slot context and show failure, but close the form without a repair action.

prompt: A patient selects a slot and confirms an appointment. What keyboard or switch behavior makes an unavailable slot and failed confirmation perceivable and recoverable?

constraints: Provider failures must be visible without blanking healthy results.
Keyboard users need to select a healthy itinerary and understand which provider did not respond.

feedback.reason: Keep healthy itineraries in a keyboard-operable list and identify the unavailable provider beside a concise status.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Treat each provider as an independent result source: retain healthy options, label unavailable sources, and keep the list’s selection operation active.
details.scenarioApplication: A traveler compares itineraries while one provider fails. Which keyboard path keeps healthy results selectable and identifies the partial failure without marking the whole search unavailable? Provider failures must be visible without blanking healthy results. Keyboard users need to select a healthy itinerary and understand which provider did not respond.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not announce total search failure while valid results remain; report partial failure alongside the remaining choices.
details.errorCorrection: A partial provider failure does not make returned itineraries unusable; replacing the list hides valid choices.
details.transfer: If a failed provider later recovers, add its results without clearing the traveler’s current selection or moving focus unexpectedly.

messages.text: A partial provider failure does not make returned itineraries unusable; replacing the list hides valid choices.
Visible but unreachable choices do not complete the keyboard task, and slow providers need not block healthy results.
A map color does not name the failed provider or explain the result state to keyboard and assistive-technology users.

options.text: Keep healthy itineraries selectable by keyboard and identify the unavailable provider with status.
Keep the provider error explicit, but replace every healthy itinerary with one failure banner.
Keep partial results visible and labeled, but remove them from keyboard focus until all providers respond.
Keep healthy results keyboard-operable, but mark provider failure only through a map color.
